match_case_results.description: exact matches through plural / prep-word normalization
match_case_results.derivation: Onions->onion, fresh thyme->thyme ('fresh' is a prep word), potatoes->potato; olive oil and vegetable stock are protected two-word terms kept whole. All 5 of 5 present: 5/5 = 1.0.

match_case_results.description: synonym matches: scallions=spring onions, white rice=rice, cilantro=coriander
match_case_results.derivation: Recipe: Chicken Salt Pepper 'Ginger Cordial' Ginger 'Spring Onions' Rice Water Coriander (9). Synonym table: spring onion(s) and scallion(s) -> green onion; white rice -> rice; coriander -> cilantro. 'ginger cordial' is not 'ginger' (extra word 'cordial' is no cut/variety), so missing (important). 8 matched / 9 = 0.8889.

match_case_results.description: specificity, pantry MORE specific: chicken thighs satisfy 'chicken' fully
match_case_results.derivation: 'chicken thigh' has every word of 'chicken' plus 'thigh', a listed cut: full match. 'Granulated sugar' resolves to sugar (synonym) and is not in the pantry; sake and potato starch absent; none has a substitution. 6 matched / 9 = 0.6667; chicken (critical) is matched, so can cook.

match_case_results.description: specificity, pantry LESS specific: generic chicken for 'chicken breast' is a partial
match_case_results.derivation: Recipe: 'Enchilada sauce' 'shredded Monterey Jack cheese' 'corn tortillas' 'chicken breasts' (4). The recipe wants 'chicken breast'; pantry 'chicken' lacks 'breast', a listed cut: partial, worth 0.7. Monterey Jack is not a cut/variety word, so the cheese is missing. (2 + 0.7)/4 = 0.675. The partial is the critical item and is NOT critical-missing.

match_case_results.description: protected term: sweet potato must not satisfy potato
match_case_results.derivation: 'sweet potato' is protected, so it is not 'potato' plus a variety word. Potatoes is the critical ingredient and is missing. base 4/5 = 0.8, minus 0.3 for one critical missing = 0.5. The score reaches the 0.5 threshold, but a critical ingredient is missing, so can_cook is False.

match_case_results.description: protected term: cream must not satisfy cream cheese
match_case_results.derivation: Recipe: Butter 'Egg Yolks'[c] 'Cream Cheese' 'Baking Powder' Flour Jam (6). Pantry 'cream' resolves through the synonym table to heavy cream, which is not cream cheese (protected). Flour resolves to all purpose flour on both sides. 5/6 = 0.8333.

match_case_results.description: protected term that can collapse: 'hot sauce' must not become plain 'sauce'
match_case_results.derivation: Recipe: Fries, 'Doner Meat', 'Garlic sauce', Hotsauce, Lettuce, Tomato, Cucumber, 'Gouda cheese' (8). Synonym table: hotsauce -> hot sauce. 'hot' is a prep modifier that normalization strips, so 'hot sauce' survives only because it is a PROTECTED term; without protection it would collapse to 'sauce' and be satisfied by the pantry's generic 'sauce'. It must not be: hot sauce is missing (important). 'Fries' singularizes to 'fry'. 7 of 8 matched = 0.875, nothing critical missing. [Replaced after the first run. The original d3_07 (pantry 'cream cheese' against a recipe's 'heavy cream') passed, but a mutation check showed it could not fail on protected-term logic: both names carry an extra word, so they never match whatever is protected. This case can fail: it is the one place PROTECTED_TERMS changes an outcome, because 'hot' is stripped as a prep word.]

match_case_results.description: protected term: spring onion (green onion) must not satisfy onion
match_case_results.derivation: spring onions -> green onion (synonym), which is protected and not 'onion' plus a variety word. Onion (important) is missing; 5/6 = 0.8333.

match_case_results.description: specificity full by colour + optional-only gaps still cook
match_case_results.derivation: 'red onion' is 'onion' plus the listed variety word 'red': full match. The two missing items are both optional, so nothing critical is missing: 4/6 = 0.6667, can cook.

match_case_results.description: substitution applied: evaporated milk for heavy cream (no restriction)
match_case_results.derivation: Substitutions: heavy cream -> evaporated milk (1:1, minimal). (5 + 0.7)/6 = 0.95.

notes: Dimension 1 baseline SUPERSEDES the earlier F1 0.64 (mistral-medium-2505) and 0.55 (ministral-8b-2512) figures. Two scorer corrections make those numbers non-comparable, and both can only lower a score: (1) a photo where the model identified nothing now counts as a zero instead of being dropped from the mean; (2) 'green onion' no longer matches ground-truth 'onion' (a scallion is not a bulb onion). A lower number than 0.55 is therefore not by itself a model regression.
Dimension 2 now enforces hand-authored constraints (eval/cases.py) in addition to what the pipeline extracted, whole-word avoid matching, and a dimension verdict that requires every case to pass.

Dimension 2 corrections after run_1793926853: expectations for d2_10, d2_12 and d2_30 were corrected (see eval/cases.py CORRECTIONS); only a user-STATED cook-time limit is enforced by the scorer, not the profile default. The pipeline changed too: stated-vs-default cook time, relaxation on 'nothing cookable', code-level avoid-list exclusion, and a deterministic dietary-restriction backstop. Compare this run to run_1793926853 with those changes in mind; they are not like-for-like.

Dimension 3 (match accuracy) checks the matcher's arithmetic against hand-derived values, 32 cases; Dimensions 4 and 5 run each case against a throwaway pantry/profile database (eval/isolation.py), reset and verified empty between cases, and fingerprint the real pantry, user and recipe databases before and after (they must be unchanged). The pass thresholds for 4 and 5 (0.80) were fixed before their first run. Dimension 5 also reports cases that passed on outcome while the system's own scoring did not reflect the profile (passed_without_scoring_support): those passes came from tie-breaking or the language model.
